messages:
anya: @channel Rolling out two things today: 1) a formal "compatibility corridor" policy for SDK releases and 2) a lightweight docs checklist we call DocShip. Goal: fewer post-release surprises for customers and clearer migration paths. Read the quick summary below and drop :eyes: or questions.

rao: nice! what's the corridor length and how does it apply to prereleases?

anya: corridor = the guaranteed compatibility window for client-facing contracts. Default: 90 days for hosted/managed SDKs, 180 days for Private deployments. It applies to GA minor releases (not to alpha/beta tags). Pre-releases should be treated as experimental and must be flagged in docs.

emily: where's DocShip? can we reuse existing migration templates?

anya: draft checklist + templates here: https://redwood.internal/docs/docship-v1 (checklist includes: migration guide template, sample snippets for major languages, QA prompt set, rollback recipe, and consumer-facing messaging). Reuse encouraged; please link your repo when you use it.

tom: quick ask from Platform: add an automated smoke test that runs the QA prompt set against canary for every SDK PR. We should gate releases on that passing.

anya: agreed. Platform + EngInfra to add a job. we also want a small harness so SDK owners can run locally.

security-bot: heads-up: telemetry for deprecation/compat events must be opt-in and PII-free. Any telemetry schema needs a security review ticket.

anya: noted. telemetry will be opt-in. field name proposed: compat_reporting_enabled. only aggregate counts and error-class buckets are collected. no request bodies, no prompts, no user ids. we'll open a security review now.

rao: how do we communicate to customers who already pinned older SDKs?

anya: Customer Success will get a pre-notice email during the corridor window with a short banner option in Console for affected customers. Private customers also get an account-team message and extended corridor automatically.

emily: minor clarification: after the corridor ends, what's the minimum notice for removal of deprecated fields?

anya: once corridor lapses, we require a 30-day public notice before removing a field from the client contract. Internal deprecation docs will keep precise timelines.

tom: can we get an example to put in the migration guide? a tiny before/after sample would help.

anya: yes. migration template includes example snippets for JS, Python, and Go. Example: 
```js
// before: v2.4
client.generate({ prompt: "...", model: "rwd-small" })
// after: v2.5 uses param name 'input' instead of 'prompt'
client.generate({ input: "...", model: "rwd-small" })
```

emily: perfect. I'll take JS + README updates. I'll add the tiny demo script that runs the QA prompt set.

docs-bot: Auto-issue created: RFC-3210; PR #4992 attached; migration-template: https://git.redwood/infra/migration-templates/sdk-migration-v2.md

security-bot: created ticket SEC-769 for telemetry schema review.

anya: timeline: policy effective next Tuesday. DocShip checklist and migration templates usable now (draft). We'll merge PR after one week of feedback and run a pilot with the JS SDK v2.5 canary release.

rao: can I volunteer to own the Go snippets?

anya: please do, Rao. assign yourself on PR.

emily: scheduling note: can we do a 30-minute sync with CS + Platform tomorrow at 11am PT to walk the checklist?

anya: 11am PT works. sending invite now.

tom: tiny UX ask: in Console banner copy, avoid the word 'deprecation'. use 'scheduled change' + link to migration guide. customers find 'deprecation' alarming.

anya: good call — we'll standardize consumer-facing wording in the DocShip messaging section; internal pages will retain the technical terms.

docs-bot: Reminder: review draft PR in 4 days.

anya: thanks all. If you're planning to contribute, leave a short note on the PR so reviewers can be assigned. Appreciate the rapid feedback.
